t: 3712. Sum of Elements With Frequency Divisible by K
o: Count how many times each value occurs; if a value's frequency is divisible by k, add value × frequency to the answer. Values are bounded by 100 and n by 100, so even an O(n²) count works, but a hash map / frequency array is cleaner. Example: in [1,2,2,3,3,3,3,4] with k=2, values 2 (freq 2) and 3 (freq 4) qualify, contributing 4 + 12 = 16.
k: Frequency divisibility is checked once per distinct value, then the whole multiplicity is added.

a.i: One pass builds a frequency map; a second pass over the map adds qualifying contributions.
s: For each (value, freq), if freq % k == 0 add value * freq.
a.t: O(n) — one pass to count, one over distinct values

a.i: Since values fit in [1,100], a plain array replaces the hash map for speed and simplicity.
s: Sum value * freq[value] for indices with freq % k == 0.

w: Trivial warm-up; mention the array trick when value ranges are small. Pitfall: adding the value only once instead of value × frequency. Follow-up: what if frequencies must be divisible by k but elements added only once?
